_comment: Bleakhold: Crucible of Onyxia (map 902), terrain v1: a 10-man custom raid laid out as one continuous map,
three legs sharing one instance lock. World X is north, Y is west (MapForge convention, see royale_v1.json).
Tile range x [31,33] y [31,32]. Note the axes: tiles.x runs along world Y and tiles.y along world X,
so the block is X -533.33..533.33 by Y -1066.67..533.33. The three legs run along Y (the long axis);
the border cliff (inset 50, width 100) eats the outer ~150 yards, so every pad stays well inside that.
Three WMO placements carry the real dungeon/raid interiors UNCHANGED: the Ragefire Chasm WMO at the west
anchor (RFC_ANCHOR) and the Onyxia's Lair WMO at the east anchor (ONY_ANCHOR). The middle leg has no WMO:
Molten Core is ADT terrain, not a model (see _molten_core below). Both WMO paths are confirmed against
the live client's archives; what still needs an in-game look is each model's real footprint ('bounds')
and its door-facing orientation, so the connective tunnels meet the doors (rebuild with --assets for the
real model boxes, as royale_v1.json's own note says).
Connective terrain between the anchors is new (the custom 20%): three flattened pads, a ramped tunnel
corridor west->centre (fire-cult cave, RFC_ANCHOR to the mid pad) and a causeway centre->east (scorched
basalt, mid pad to ONY_ANCHOR), closed by a border cliff ring so nobody falls off the map edge (royale's
'no holes: players drop in anywhere' approach, since this is a raid with a fixed entrance not a BG drop).
pois feed the raid's boss/trash anchor SQL the way bh_royale_poi feeds Royale's POI table (package.py
writes it): 'entrance' is the raid's start point, 'intro_boss' the RFC-leg custom boss spot, 'final_boss'
Onyxia's own spot inside her WMO (z_from the WMO, like royale's crate z_from), 'trash_anchor' points mark
where leg trash spawns cluster (consumed when the SQL for Phase 2 is written; harmless if package.py's
current POI kind set doesn't know these names yet -- that validation is Royale-specific per the README).
Every non-WMO texture path below is a verified stock 3.3.5a path (lava/basalt/ash tilesets used all over
Blackrock Mountain content); only the three wmo 'model' paths need VPS verification.

areas._: the Scorched Causeway (mid leg, no WMO)

features._: RFC_ANCHOR pad: a shallow scorched bowl, entrance faces east into the tunnel
the mid pad: a wide basalt shelf in Molten Core's register, the raid's midpoint
ONY_ANCHOR pad: Onyxia's bowl mouth, slightly sunken for the dragon's lair feel
tunnel corridor RFC->MC: a sunken scorched-rock ramp
causeway MC->Onyxia: a wider basalt path, lava-flanked
shallow lava-adjacent gullies either side of the causeway
closing ring, outer foothill: a jittered rise up to the cliff foot (same two-ring form as royale_v1)
closing ring, inner wall: a short steep cliff (height 60 over width 20 is ~72 deg, past the 50 deg walkable limit) so nobody climbs or swims out; one fixed entrance, no gaps needed

texture_rules._: regional: scorched grass fringe around the RFC pad
global: rock on steep ground (border cliffs)

_comment: Ragefire Chasm. Its client name is the Orgrimmar Lava Dungeon, which is why nothing called 'ragefire'
exists: path confirmed from the live client's archives (list_client_files.py over common.MPQ).
Facing and the exact position still need a look in game: the model carries its own entrance, so the
connective tunnel's mouth (the ramp from RFC_ANCHOR towards the mid pad) has to meet that door.
wmos.label: RFC_ANCHOR

_comment: Onyxia's Lair, the main cavern. The client holds KL_OnyxiasLair.wmo, _A and _B; only _A and _B are
referenced by the game (both are in the realm's extracted vmaps, the bare one is not), and _B is the
large hall (441 KB of vmap against _A's 158 KB), so _B is the lair the raid ends in. _A (the entrance
stretch) can be added beside it once the two are seen together in game: their relative offset comes
from map 249's own placement, which is not copied here.
Facing and position need the same in-game check as the RFC anchor.
wmos.label: ONY_ANCHOR

_molten_core: There is no Molten Core WMO. The client's whole Dungeon\ WMO tree was listed and MC is not in it; the
AZ_Blackrock models are Blackrock Depths (_lower_) and Blackrock Spire (_upper_). Molten Core is built
from ADT terrain on its own map (409), so it cannot be placed as a model the way RFC and Onyxia are.
The middle leg is therefore MapForge's own lava terrain in MC's register (the lavarock/ash texturing and
the sunken gullies flanking the causeway below), not MC's actual rooms. Importing MC's real geometry
would mean copying its ADT tiles, which this generator does not do.
